clue.text: Call for book section

definitions.meaning: to summon someone over a public address system, as in a hotel or hospital
one leaf or side of a book's paper

explanation.surface: A request to look up a passage in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: summoning someone by loudspeaker, and a single sheet of a book.

clue.text: Old actor, getting wiser over time

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the word for wiser is laid round the time letter

parts.note: wiser means sager, more sage

explanation.surface: An elderly performer who has grown wiser with the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a container signal: SAGER covers T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stager is an archaic word for a stage player, surviving in the phrase 'old stager' for a veteran.

clue.text: What's really important in part of Shakespearean player's speech

definitions.meaning: the crucial or deciding factor in a matter
a line spoken by Bottom, the weaver who acts in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Picking out the crucial part of an actor's lines in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the amateur actor in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so one of his lines is part of his speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the essential point or deciding factor in any matter.

clue.text: Leftie somewhat short, if hugged by supporter

indicators.note: something hugged by another is held inside it, so the trimmed phrase goes within the fan word

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: short means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: A left-winger who is a little short if a backer embraces him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the phrase for 'somewhat' and 'hugged by' signals a container; 'if' only links. The Fabian Society is a long-standing British socialist think tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Fabian Society are British socialists, so left-wingers.

clue.text: Consider penning lines, any number almost

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep are penned, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to weigh something up is to consider it
L is an abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Weighing up the writing of a few lines, with almost any amount involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' reads as writing, beside 'lines', but signals enclosure, as sheep are penned.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is an old-fashioned synonym for nearly or virtually.

clue.text: Worst as one part of speech, but only one

definitions.text: Worst as one part of speech, but only one

parts.words: Worst as one part of speech, but only one
parts.note: as a verb, to worst someone is to defeat them, a synonym of the answer; but as an adjective the two are opposites, so they match in one part of speech only

explanation.surface: A grammar note on how a word behaves in different roles.
explanation.walkthrough: As adjectives they are opposite superlatives; as verbs both mean defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst and to best an opponent both mean to beat them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: It's a shock, a bad actor turning up as prince

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock
a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: A shocking moment as a poor performer appears in the role of a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AJARAHAM, the string built from A, JAR, A and HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is an Indian ruling prince.

clue.text: Supposed cause of global revolution, some rising

definitions.text: Supposed cause of global revolution, some rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the taken letters read upwards
some means only part of the word revolution is taken

explanation.surface: A theory about what makes the world turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes EVOL from revolution; 'rising' turns it round. The whole clue alludes to the saying that it makes the world go round.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says it is affection that makes the world go round, hence the supposed cause of the globe turning.

clue.text: Measuring device in a store rebuilt outside research site

indicators.note: outside means the reworked letters sit around the other piece
rebuilt means the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: a lab, laboratory, is a site for research

explanation.surface: An instrument found in a shop that was rebuilt beyond a research facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' turns A STORE into ASTROE, which 'outside' wraps around LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an old instrument for measuring the altitude of stars.

clue.text: Elegist's initial reaction, oddly his inspiration?

indicators.note: initial means only the first letter of the word Elegist's
oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word reaction

explanation.surface: A writer of elegies reacts first, perhaps oddly, to what inspires him.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry, so a fitting source of inspiration for an elegist.

clue.text: American serving in the westbound crew

indicators.note: in an across entry westbound means reading right to left
a soldier serving in a unit is inside it, so the American goes within the word the

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A US serviceman stationed with a team heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving in' signals a container, making THGIE, and 'westbound' suits an across entry, read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat's team of eight oarsmen is itself called an eight.

clue.text: Tense speaker will, with a banterer

parts.note: the speaker saying 'I will' contracts it to I'll, written without the apostrophe
a tease is someone who banters or mocks playfully

explanation.surface: A nervous orator shares the stage with a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like grammar beside 'will'; it is the adjective meaning anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease is an idiom for being uncomfortable or nervous.

clue.text: One of a dozen in a box, in case?

definitions.text: One of a dozen in a box, in case?

parts.words: One of a dozen in a box, in case?
parts.note: suggests eggs in a carton, but means one of twelve people seated in the jury box during a legal case

explanation.surface: An item packed in a box of twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is the jury box and the case is a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury traditionally has twelve members, who sit in the jury box hearing a court case.

clue.text: See 24
Charge misbehaving child in front of a head

indicators.note: in front of places the child word before the other piece

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
per head means each, so a head means each

explanation.surface: Blaming a naughty child before a headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' means per person, as in 'five pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to formally accuse an official of wrongdoing.

clue.text: In group, oddly gain by taking revenge

indicators.note: In at the start means the reworked letters go inside the group word

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves

indicators.note: oddly means the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A gang member strangely profiting from vengeance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an alternate-letters signal but rearranges GAIN BY into YINGBA, which goes inside PACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying someone back is an idiom for getting even with them.

clue.text: Stop for travellers before India, as pilot says

definitions.meaning: a place where people on a journey stay the night
in the NATO phonetic alphabet used by pilots, the word for H comes just before India for I

explanation.surface: A traveller's rest stop on the way to India, as the pilot announces.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a lodging for travellers and the radio code word for the letter H.

clue.text: Sources of water selfish protester cut before one

indicators.note: before puts the shortened word ahead of the letter for one
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a NIMBY ('not in my back yard') objects to developments near their own home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A self-interested campaigner cuts off the water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims NIMBY to NIMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are rain clouds, the plural of nimbus, so they supply rain.

clue.text: Daisy's relative's crazy over crazy girl about love

indicators.note: over means covering, so the word for crazy wraps the rest

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters surround the love letter
crazy here means the letters of girl are jumbled

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A girl called Daisy has a relative who is utterly mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'crazy' jumbles the girl into RIGL, 'about' wraps it round the love letter, and 'over' sets that under the first crazy word. Daisy is the flower, not a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a plant of the daisy family, Asteraceae.

clue.text: Key producer playing role of leader in Hollywood

parts.note: an actor appears as a character, so playing the role of means as

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A performer cast as the head of a film studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is not a piano or lock key but a winged seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree's winged seeds are called keys, so it produces them.

clue.text: To tell the truth in a court, you reported friend

indicators.note: reported means the word is to be heard, not written

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Giving honest testimony in court about a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' joining the pieces is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are sentence adverbs meaning in fact or truthfully.

clue.text: Cause of ferment coming from unknown quarter

parts.note: Y is an unknown quantity in algebra
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Unrest stirring in an unexpected part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ferment' suggests political unrest but means fermentation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that makes dough and brews ferment.

clue.text: Point in what we do with the Web too much

indicators.note: in means the compass point is placed within the phrase

parts.words: what we do with the Web
parts.note: we surf the internet, that is, surf it
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A remark on spending excessive time online.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess or overabundance of something.

clue.text: Permission to leave a learner in set

parts.note: a congé is formal leave to depart
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A trainee in a class is given leave to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a group the learner is in; it is the verb meaning harden.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to solidify or thicken, as jelly sets.

clue.text: Kittenish cat not finishing rodents

parts.note: kittenish means playfully coy

indicators.note: not finishing means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: A playful cat leaves its rodent prey unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' cuts PUSS to PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Coypus are large South American water rodents.

clue.text: Strikingly colourful contents of sexy notice

indicators.note: contents of means each word loses its outer letters and keeps what lies within

explanation.surface: A racy advertisement in bright colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic plumage or flowers are vivid and unusual, a common sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Worthy work at home, holding evaluation back

indicators.note: holding means the home-work word encloses the other piece

parts.note: DIY, do it yourself, is home improvement work

indicators.note: back means the evaluation word is written backwards

parts.note: a rating is an evaluation

explanation.surface: A worthwhile job done at home, with assessment held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worthy' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a notable person; 'back' gives GNITAR and 'holding' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthy is a noun for a notable person, as is a dignitary.

clue.text: Jack, in navy, does otherwise, in nautical spirit

indicators.note: in means the Jack letter goes within the rearranged letters
otherwise means the letters are set out differently

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A sailor in the navy behaves differently under a sea spirit's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges NAVY DOES as DAVYONES; 'in' puts J inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailors' folklore, the named figure is the evil spirit of the sea whose locker is the seabed.

clue.text: Part in Pride movie, as just quoted

indicators.note: part in means a run of letters lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An actor's role in the film Pride, cited again.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for the same, used in references for the source just cited.

clue.text: Split agreed between Britain and EU? Not half!

indicators.note: between means the agreed word sits between the two other pieces
not half means only one of the two letters, the first

parts.note: OK means agreed

explanation.surface: Brexit as a deal splitting Britain and the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' also reads as British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke is the past tense of break, meaning split or broke apart.

clue.text: Nervous and at the forefront of fashion

definitions.meaning: cutting-edge or provocatively modern in style

explanation.surface: An anxious trendsetter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both anxious and boldly avant-garde.

clue.text: So long screening very old television part

indicators.note: screening means hiding, so the farewell word encloses the other letter

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell while showing a very old TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' suggests television but signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Old television sets used thermionic tubes, called valves in Britain, as components.

clue.text: Setting up key in having a meal

indicators.note: in means the key letter goes inside the meal word

parts.note: lunching means having lunch
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Launching a venture over a business lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a project is to start it up or establish it.
